description:
Privateering

About

Reworks commissions to be a less passive, becoming a more active element within your playthrough.
This is done through rebalancing commissions, adding a new resource called requisition bonds, and adding a small event-based progression system for commissions.
The mod can be added mid-save. Not all updates are save compatible, check the changelog for details on if they are.

Not compatible with "Ashes of the Domain - Questions of Loyalty". Other ashes modules are compatible.
The mod requires LunaLib, MagicLib and GraphicsLib

Requisition Bonds

Requisition bonds are a new resource accquired after defeating fleets hostile to your commissioned faction.
Bonds can only be spent by visiting your commission supervisor, who is a new contract that you will find in one of the factions major colonies.
They can be freely exchanged in to services like custom production, repairing dmods or hiring mercenaries, but they can not be converted to credits.

Commission Rebalance

Commissions within the base game provide you with a lot of passive income.
From the start they provide 25000 credits per month, at maximum they give 95000 per month.
To me, this can easily help diminish the feeling of having had to work for what i have within the game..

As such, within the mod the monthly payment is reduced to a non-scaling 15000 credits per month.
In addition, it introduces a new method of support however. Commissions will now pay 50% of your fleet maintenance costs for you.
This includes monthly supplies, crew and officers. Each of those has their own cap, combining with the base pay to at most 50000 credits per month, but only if you already have a larger fleet.

Favorability

The mod adds a small progression event when joining a commission. Defeating opponents will improve your favor with the faction you work with.
This provides small, but useful benefits as you stay with the faction, but not large enough that you would never want to leave.

Frequently asked Questions

Does this mod make the game harder?
It is not intended to be, while there are nerfs to existing systems, the new systems are supposed to make up for them.
As the mod is still new, it may need some more tweaking though.

Is this compatible with faction mods?
The mod should work for all faction mods without issue.

Should i use Privateering or Questions of Loyalty?
As Questions of Loyalty is incompatible with this mod, you have to choose either it or Privateering.
Privateering is a simple rework of the system, keeping it close to vanillas intentions, but modifying and adding bits and pieces here.
Questions of Loyalty may be more to your liking if you prefer a large revamp, changing commissions in to a long time commitment.

Support

If you want to support my work, you can do so on Patreon.
You can also follow me there for free for blog posts and progress updates.
Any level of support is deeply appreciated!

discordPostHtml:
A simple overhaul to faction commissions.
The goal of the mod is to add a few more features to commissions while making them feel less "passive" overall.

Latest Download: https://github.com/Lukas22041/Privateering/releases/latest/download/Privateering.zip
Forum Post: https://fractalsoftworks.com/forum/index.php?topic=33914

Commission Rebalance
Vanilla commissions scale by level, with the formula being 20000 + (5000*level) , maxing at 95k credits per month.
This mod reduces the basic pay to a measly non-scaling 15k credits per month.
The catch is that certain maintenance costs, like supplies and officers, now have 50% of their upkeep covered by your faction.

Requisition Bonds
Requisition bonds are a new resource. They are accquired when fighting fleets hostile to your commission faction.
A bond is equal to 500 credits, but can only be spent by meeting with your commission supervisor.
The supervisor is a new NPC which has several options for spending bonds like custom production, hiring mercs and repairing d-mods.

Favorability
The mod adds a new major event, called Faction Favorability.
As you support the faction, you gain more favor with it, resulting in being rewarded with slight bonuses.

-Not compatible with AoTD - Questions of Loyalty 
-Works fine with other Ashes modules.
